questions: Should the output integers a and b be printed on the same line separated by a space, or on separate lines?
Are the rows of the grids given without any spaces between characters, exactly as a continuous string of N (or M) characters per line?
Is the indexing of a and b 1‑based as described, and must the printed values also be 1‑based?
If multiple positions satisfy the condition (contrary to the guarantee), which one should be output?
Are there any trailing newline or whitespace requirements after printing a and b?
Can the input contain extra blank lines or leading/trailing spaces that need to be ignored?
Must the program handle the case where N = M = 1, i.e., a single cell grid?
Are there any time or memory limits that could affect the choice of algorithm for the given constraints?
answers: a and b are printed on one line, separated by a single space.

inline_prompts:
You are given an N \times N grid S and an M \times M grid T. The cell at the i-th row from the top and the j-th column from the left is denoted by (i,j).
The colors of the cells in S and T are represented by N^2 characters S_{i,j} (1\leq i,j\leq N) and M^2 characters T_{i,j} (1\leq i,j\leq M), respectively. In grid S, cell (i,j) is white if S_{i,j} is ., and black if S_{i,j} is #. The same applies for grid T.
Find T within S. More precisely, output integers a and b (1 \leq a,b \leq N-M+1) that satisfy the following condition:
- S_{a+i-1,b+j-1} = T_{i,j} for every i,j (1\leq i,j \leq M).
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N M
S_{1,1}S_{1,2}\dots S_{1,N}
S_{2,1}S_{2,2}\dots S_{2,N}
\vdots
S_{N,1}S_{N,2}\dots S_{N,N}
T_{1,1}T_{1,2}\dots T_{1,M}
T_{2,1}T_{2,2}\dots T_{2,M}
\vdots
T_{M,1}T_{M,2}\dots T_{M,M}
Output
Print a and b.
Constraints
- 1 \leq M \leq N \leq 50
- N and M are integers.
- Each of S_{i,j} and T_{i,j} is . or #.
- There is exactly one pair (a,b) satisfying the condition.
